1. Raw Material
Raw materials serve as the fundamental base for manufacturing. They are essential for initiating the production of the die pl ate and
form the core of a robust industrial process.
2. CNC Process
CNC machining is used to shape the raw material using pre -programmed computer instructions. This ensures precise, consistent,
and efficient shaping of the die plate’s geometry.
3. VMC Process
The Vertical Machining Center (VMC) performs advanced operations like milling and drilling. With a vertical spindle, it enabl es
the creation of detailed and accurate features on the die plate.
4. Brazing Process
The brazing process achieved in a vacuum environment. This fuses the components without melting the base metal, ensuring strong
joints. Vacuum furnaces installed at the unit is electrically heated, flameless and operates under vacuum conditions, generat ing no
air emissions, no flue gas and no waste water. Entire process of brazing is clean and non -polluting.
5. Electric Drilling Machine Process
This stage uses an electric motor -powered drill to create holes in the die plate. The process involves proper bit selection and
controlled downward pressure for precise hole formation.
6. Wire Cut Process
Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machining) uses a thin wire to cut complex shapes. A dielectric fluid and CNC motion control
enable precise machining of hard materials in the die plate.
7. Nickel Coating (Final Stage)
Electroless nickel plating is applied as a final protective layer. The die plate is immersed in a solution containing nickel salts and a
reducing agent, forming a uniform nickel -phosphorus coating that enhances corrosion and wear resistance. We don't have this
facility in-house therefore we outsource this job.
Blade Flow Manufacturing Process
1. Raw Material
Raw materials are the base components required to manufacture the blade. These are essential building blocks that support all
subsequent processes and are crucial to maintaining a strong industrial base.
2. Wire Cut Process
This process uses Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machining), where a thin wire acts as the electrode. It precisely cuts compl ex
shapes from hard materials like tungsten carbide using CNC-controlled motion and dielectric fluid for accuracy.
3. Grinding Process

Grinding is a precision operation that removes excess material using an abrasive wheel or belt. This ensures a smooth surface finish
and accurate dimensions, preparing the blade for further stages.
4. Electric Drilling Machine Process
Holes are created using an electric motor -driven drill. This involves choosing the right bit, fixing the workpiece, and drilling with
rotating motion and pressure to achieve the desired depth and diameter.
5. Wire Cut Process (Repeated)
Wire EDM is again used to perform additional complex cuts required for the final blade shape or features. This repetition ens ures
intricate geometries are accurately produced.
6. Slitting Process
This is a variant of wire cut EDM, where electric discharges are used to slice or split material with high precision. It is used to create
narrow cuts or divisions within the blade structure.
7. Grinding Process (Repeated)
A final grinding stage ensures that surface quality and dimensional tolerances meet the final product standards. This guarant ees a
refined and accurate finish.
8. Finish Product
After completing all machining and shaping stages, the blade is ready as a finished product, meeting quality and functional standards.
Blade Holder Manufacturing Process
1. Raw Material
Raw materials are the essential building blocks used to manufacture the blade holder. These foundational substances support t he
entire production process and are critical to maintaining a strong industrial base.
2. CNC Process (Main Body)
CNC machining uses pre -programmed instructions to operate machine tools such as mills and lathes. This ensures the main body
of the blade holder is shaped precisely and efficiently with high accuracy.
3. CNC Process (Centre Part)
Similar to the main body, the centre part is manufactured using CNC technology. The automation allows repeatable, high -speed
shaping tailored for this specific section of the holder.
4. CNC Process (Centre Ring)

The centre ring is machined using CNC tools to meet tight dimensional requirements. The computer -controlled process enhances
precision and consistency across batches.
5. VMC Process (Centre Part)
A Vertical Machining Center (VMC) is used to further refine the centre part. This process enables detailed operations like mi lling,
drilling, and tapping with a vertical spindle, ensuring component accuracy.
6. VMC Process (Centre Ring)
The centre ring is processed using VMC machinery to perform precise shaping and finishing operations, making it ready for
integration with other components.
7. VMC Process (Cutter Body)
The cutter body undergoes VMC machining, which ensures clean finishes and complex shape creation with precision, preparing it
for functional use.
8. Wire Cut Process
In this stage, Wire EDM (Electrical Discharge Machining) is employed. A thin wire cuts through hard materials to create intri cate
profiles. A dielectric fluid helps maintain accuracy during this precise operation.
9. Drilling Process
Circular holes are made in the components using rotating drill bits. This hole -making process is essential for enabling fasteners or
further assembly alignment in the final product.
10. Assembly
All the individual components —main body, centre part, centre ring, and cutter body —are joined together. This involves handling
the parts, aligning them properly, and fitting them to form the final blade holder.
11. Final Product
After all machining and assembly stages, the completed blade holder is ready for deployment or shipment.
Driving Bush Flow Manufacturing Process
1. Raw Material
The manufacturing process begins with raw materials—fundamental substances used to construct the driving bush. These materials
form the base structure for further machining and assembly.
2. CNC Process (Cover)
CNC machining uses pre -programmed software to control machines, shaping the cover portion of the driving bush with high
accuracy and repeatability. This ensures a consistent and precise outcome.

4. VMC Process (Cover)
A Vertical Machining Center (VMC) is employed to perform operations like drilling, tapping, and milling on the cover. The vertical

The shaft also undergoes VMC operations, enhancing precision and surface quality. This ensures the shaft matches exact

sections.heading: OUR TRADING PROCESS
sections.text:
1. PO Copy (our client PO):
The process begins with receiving a Purchase Order (PO) from our client. This document outlines the items, quantities, and te rms
of the order. It serves as the formal request for goods or services and initiates the procurement process.
2. Enquiry for trading items:
Upon receiving the PO, we raise an inquiry for the required trading items. This involves reaching out to potential suppliers to
check availability, prices, lead times, and commercial terms. The objective is to identify the best possible sourcing options .
3. Received offer against Inquiry:
Suppliers respond to our inquiry with offers containing detailed quotations. These offers include pricing, delivery schedules ,
payment terms, and technical specifications, if any. We evaluate these offers to choose the most suitable vendor.
4. Place PO to supplier:
After finalizing the offer, we issue a Purchase Order to the selected supplier. This PO confirms our intention to buy the spe cified
items under agreed terms. It is a binding document that ensures timely procurement.

documents are shared to ensure timely and safe delivery.

sections.heading: OUR COMPETITIVE STRENGTH
sections.text:
Experienced Promoters and Management Team.
The Promoters of our Company ha ve significant in-depth knowledge of the industry and has been instrumental in the consistent
growth of our Company’s performance. They both have a good experience of industry. We believe that our promoter’s experience
and their understanding of the business will enable us to continue to take advantage of both current and future market opportunities.
They are playing vital role in formulating business strategies and effective implementation of the same, thus, managing the overall
business operations of the Co mpany. Our Promoters share various functional responsibilities amongst themselves for effective
management and are also well supported by experienced staff at different levels.
Existing client relationship.
We are committed to consistently addressing our customer’s needs regarding our products. We prioritize meeting specific customer
requirements and timely order delivery as fundamental factors for our company's growth. Our company has consistently strived to
ensure customer satisfaction by actively taking measures to meet customer demand, ensuring timely order fulfilment, and
maintaining consistent product quality. As a result, we have seen a strong client relationship that demonstrate the trust placed in us
by our customers. We provide comprehensive after -sales service and assure our customers that should they encounter any quality
issues with our products; we will facilitate returns.
Quality Service.
We believe in providing quality and timely service to our customers. We have set very high standards for ourselves when it co mes
to timelines and quality of service we provide to our customers. The stringent systems ensure that all the products reach our
customers on stipulated time and there are minimum errors to ensure reduced product rejection. We believe that our quality service
has earned us a goodwill from our customers, which has resulted in customer retention and order repetition. It has also helped us to
add to our existing customer base. Our company focuses on maintaining the level of consistently in our service, thereby build ing
customer loyalty for our Brand.
Well established systems and procedures
Our organization prides itself on its robust systems and procedures meticulously designed for the seamless implementation of both
machinery and manpower to achieve current and long -term objectives. Through a comprehensive approach, we ensure that every
170
aspect of production, from manufacturing to final product, is optimized for efficiency and quality. Our machinery is carefull y
selected and maintained to meet industry standards, enhancing productivity and minimizing downtime. Simultaneously, our
workforce is trained extensively to operate these machines proficiently, fostering a culture of expertise and innovation.
Revenue from multiple geographies:
Our product portfolio and quality assurance has helped us establish strong relationships with our major customers. Our Compan y
has diversified revenue from multiple geographical locations across India and a portion of revenue from outside India from mo re
than 20 countries such as the USA, Germany, Netherland, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Indonesia, Japan, Luxembourg, Vietnam,
Italy, Switzerland, Austria, South Africa, Australia, Thailand, etc. We have generated around 15.27%, 17.57% and 19.62% of our
total revenue from operations from domestic sales for the fiscal year ending 2026, 2025 and 2024 respectively and generated around
84.73%, 82.43% and 80.38% of our total revenue from operation from export sales for the for the fiscal year ending 2026, 2025
and 2024 respectively. Currently, we market our products to more than 25 countries and gradually we intend to expand our business
operations to other geographical locations as well. This consistent growth underscores our commitment to exploring new
opportunities and strengthening our global reach. Our presence in multiple geographies not only helps us in expanding our customer
base but also helps us by keeping ourselves in tune with the latest technological advancements world -wide and help us to mitigate
risk for any unforeseen circumstances in the domestic market and expand our business operations. For the Fiscal year 2026, 2025
and 2024, our top 10 customers contributed approximately 65.71%, 73.03% and 70.45% of our revenue from operations
respectively.
Customized Product Offering
The company tailors its product portfolio to meet customer specifications, offering various kind of blade holder’s / cutter h ub is
straight, and inclined geometry, including custom build designs for all kind of underwater pelletizers and water ring pelleti zers.
This customization capability ensures that resources are allocated efficiently to produce products that are in demand, maximi zing
profitability and minimizing waste.
In-House Research and development capabilities
We place a strong emphasis on R&D pursuant to our deep commitment to innovation. we operate in house R&D unit. Our in-house
R&D unit is dedicated to a specific business vertical. Our R&D efforts focus on innovation across product features, manufacturing
efficiency, and sustainability to meet the evolving needs of original equipment manufacturer customers. Key areas of explorat ion
include additive manufacturing, energy-efficient systems, and precision engineering, with an emphasis on reliability and reducing
environmental impact. By investing in machinery, advanced simulation techniques, and automation technologies, we aim to provide
innovative and efficient mechanical engineering solutions that align with global industry trends.
Die plates are the core component of an underwater pelletizing system, molten polymer is forced through precisely engineered
holes in the plate and cut into uniform pellets. The performance of the whole system depends on the design and finish of Die plates
and its components . During the year the Company ran development work across nine projects, spanning oil -heated die plates,
carbide tipped plates, large-format plates and cutting blades for large die plates. However, our R&D project remained the D -500
(720 x 102 mm) Oil-Heated Die Plate. The D -500 (720 x 102 mm), Oil Heated Pelletizing Die Plate is a critical component used
in pelletizing systems for graphite based polystyrene extrusion processing industries in Europe and cold climate countries.
We continue to invest in research and tools, allocating budgets for advanced tools, training, and talent acquisition. By prov iding
our engineers with the requisite resources, we aim to enable faster innovation and the resolution of complex problems. Going
forward, we intend to expand our product portfolio by initiating in-house manufacturing of 1.6-meter diameter die plates, as against
the die plates of up to 0.5-meter diameter currently offered by us. We believe that this initiative, if successfully implemented, may
strengthen our presence in the die plate manufacturing segment and support our overall business growth strategy

sections.heading: BUSINESS STRATEGY
sections.text:
Expansion of our production capacity
To meet the rising demand for our products, we are expanding our production capacity by investing in advanced machineries. Th is
will enable us to scale our operations, reduce delivery times, and serve a broader range of customer needs more efficiently. Our
product range includes pelletizing die plates, pelletizing blades/knives, blade holders/cutter hub, tapped driving bush for underwater
pelletizing systems and other spare items used across various industrial applications.
Increasing Operational efficiency
Improving efficiency is an important part of our growth plan. We are setting up a new manufacturing facility and using updated
technologies to make our production process smoother, reduce waste, and improve output. These steps help us use our resources
more effectively and support future growth. We also follow regular quality checks to help ensure that our produ cts meet industry
requirements. With these improvements, we aim to respond to customer needs more quickly, manage costs better, and continue
171
offering reliable products and services.
Growing Export Potential
We sell our products in more than 10 States & Union Territories in India and also export our products to more than 25 countries
such as the USA, Germany, Netherland, Israel, Saudi Arabia, Oman, Indonesia, Japan, Luxembourg, Vietnam, Italy, Switzerland,
Austria, South Africa, Australia, Thailand , etc. and we plan to continue our strategy of diversifying and expanding our presence in
other countries as well as other untouched regions within the country for the growth of our business. We intend to focus on
penetrating further in existing markets with an appetite for increased demand and high growth potential. Over the years of experience
and successful growth in our core markets, we believe that we are well positioned to take advantage of the growth potential and
opportunities offered to further expand our market share. We are selective in expanding to new locations and look at new geographies
where we can deliver our products without experiencing significant delays and interruptions. Through further diversification of our
operations geographically, we hope to hedge against risks of operations in only specific areas and protection from fluctuatio ns
resulting from business concentration in limited geographical areas. We intend to cater to the increasing demand of our exist ing
customers and also to increase our existing customer base by enhancing the reach of our products in different parts of the co untry
and world. We aim to achieve this by adding value to our customers through quality assurance, timely delivery and reliability .
Maintaining cordial relationship with our Suppliers and Customer
We believe in maintaining long standing relationship with our suppliers and customers which are the most important factor to keep
our Company growing. Our efficient and timely delivery of products has helped us build strong relationships with our existing
customers over a number of years. Further, we believe that establishing strong, mutually beneficial long -term relationships with
suppliers is a critical step in improving performance across the supply chain, generating cost efficiency and enabling the bu siness
to grow and develop. Longer association with employees will help in enhanced productivity and efficiency with reduced trainin g

sections.heading: RESEARCH AND DEVELOPMENT PROGRAMME
sections.text:
As we are engaged in manufacturing of high-precision die plates and related components used in underwater pelletizing systems for
the polymer -processing industry . Such products require precision and stringent quality testing, backed by our research and
development (“R&D”) capabilities. Our R&D unit, integrated within our Manufacturing Facility, are focused on developing new
product features, optimizing manufacturing processes, and advancing performance and sustainability of products to meet evolving
needs of our customers. As of now, we have in-house R&D team comprising employees from our Design, Operations and Quality
Control team, lead by Mr. Rajkumar Chaudhary, Chairman & Managing Director, who directly contributed to this R&D through his
technical expertise and dedicated personal involvement. In FY 2025-26, the company has made total Rs. 151.69 Lakhs expenditure
towards R&D work. We believe we have the capability to establish new verticals and product categories efficiently .
During the Financial Year 2025 -26, the Company ran development work across nine projects, spanning oil -heated die plates,
carbide-tipped plates, large -format plates and cutting blades for large die plates. However, our R&D project remained the D -500
(720 x 102 mm) Oil-Heated Die Plate. The D-500 (720 x 102 mm), Oil Heated Pelletizing Die Plate is a critical component used in
pelletizing systems for graphite based polystyrene extrusion processing industries in Europe and cold climate countries .
Alongside the D-500 (720 x 102 mm), the Company developed two carbide-tipped Ferro-TIC plates (SP-70 and SP-100). This was
basically a significant improvement breakthrough in an existing product aimed at longer useful life. This was an experiment t o
improve the hardness of the standard die plates and consequently the life of the plate without affecting its characteristics. Experiment
started with TIC-128 and then TIC-Nicrodur and finally after several trials, we arrived at the Ferrotic (F-TIC) which gave our desired
results, i.e hardness of the plate was improved without affecting other vital parameters. This will increase the life expectancy of the
die plate and would prove a cost -effective, durable product for the OEM giving us an edge over other manufactu rers dealing only
with the standard products.
Besides experimenting on large size die plates, we are also experimenting on large size Blades to be mounted on these large s ize
die plates. We are also experimenting with vacuum based design with the standard product SP -100. Until now we were using air
gap design. We experienced that with the air gap design, the back pressure gets increased causing uneven distribution of temperature
leading to frequent hole freezing.
With the success of D-500 (720 x 102 mm), we are encouraged to experimenting with another large size die plate D-500 (845 x 100
mm) to scale the D-500 design to a larger plate diameter. This experiment extends the D-500 platform to larger format.

During FY 2025-26, R&D work is more than a set of individual products. It builds a capability, and that capability creates several
reinforcing benefits:

• A niche, import -substitution segment : high-precision die plates of this kind, particularly for graphite -polystyrene
pelletizing, have largely been imported from European manufacturers. A locally engineered product to comparable
specification is a genuine import-substitution opportunity, and the Company's work positions MESL among the few Asian
manufacturers able to serve this segment
• Higher value, limited competition : precision-engineered die plates and the move into smaller hole sizes (down to 0.6
mm) and large-format plates sit in a higher-value segment where competition is limited.
• Capability that compounds : every project completed this year leaves behind a design baseline, proven process
parameters, tooling and supplier relationships. The next variant in each family; a different hole count, a different size, a
different polymer, can be developed at a fraction of the cost and time of the first. The Ferro -TIC hardness work, for
example, improves the durability of an entire product line without changing its core characteristics.
• Stronger market position : completing work of this difficulty changes what the Company can credibly quote for,
strengthens its standing with existing customers, and is already generating enquiries from OEMs.

sections.text:

the current provisions of Indian law, and the judicial and administrative interpretations thereof, which are subject to chang e or
modification by subsequent legislative, regulatory, administrative or judicial decisions and may not be exhaustive, and are only
intended to provide general information to investors and is neither designed nor intended to be a substitute for professional legal
advice. We are subject to a number of Central and State legislations which regulate substantive and procedural aspects of the
business. Additionally, the business activities of our Company require sanctions, approval, license, registration etc. from t he
concerned authorities, under the relevant Central and State legislations and local bye -laws. For details of Gove rnment and Other
Statutory Approvals obtained by the Company in compliance with these regulations, see chapter titled “Government and Other
Statutory Approvals” on page 249 of this Draft Red Herring Prospectus. The following is an overview of some of the i mportant
laws, policies and regulations which are pertinent to our business as a player in designing, development, manufacturing, and
refurbishment of key components used in underwater pelletizing systems for the polymer and plastics processing industry.

sections.heading: INDUSTRY SPECIFIC REGULATIONS
sections.text:
THE MICRO, SMALL AND MEDIUM ENTERPRISES DEVELOPMENT ACT, 2006
In order to promote and enhance the competitiveness of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise ("MSME") the Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006 is enacted. A National Board shall be appointed and established by the Central
Government for M SME enterprises with its head office at Delhi in the case of the enterprises engaged in the manufacture or
production of goods pertaining to any industry mentioned in the first schedule to the Industries (Development and Regulation) Act,
1951. The Governme nt, in the Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises, has issued a notification dated March 21, 2025
revising the definition and criterion and the same came into effect from April 01, 2025. The notification revised the definit ions as
“Micro enterprise”, where the investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed two crore fifty lakh rupees and
turnover does not exceed ten crore rupees; “Small enterprise”, where the investment in plant and machinery or equipment does not
exceed twenty five crore rupees and turnover does not exceed one hundred crore rupees; “Medium enterprise”, where the investment
in plant and machinery or equipment does not exceed one hundred twenty five crore rupees and turnover does not exceed five
hundred crore rupees.
NATIONAL STEEL POLICY, 2017 (“NSP 2017”)
The NSP 2017 seeks to enhance domestic steel production with focus on creating a technologically advanced and globally
competitive steel industry in India that promotes economic growth. The NSP 2017 aims to creating environment for attain ing
(i) Self-sufficiency in steel production by providing policy support and guidance to private manufacturers, MSME stee l
producers, CPSEs and encourage adequate capacity additions; (ii) Development of globally competitive steel manufacturing
capabilities; (iii) Cost-efficient production and domestic availability of iron ore, coking coal and natural gas; (iv) Facilitate
investment in overseas asset acquisitions of raw materials; and (v) Enhance domestic steel demand . The intent is to strengthen
the research and development of national importance in the iron and steel sector by utilizing tripartite synergy among indust ry,
national research and development laboratories and academic institutions. The NSP 2 017 covers, inter alia, steel demand, steel
capacity, raw materials, including iron ore iron ore pellets, manganese ore, chromite ore, ferro -alloys, land, water, power,
infrastructure and logistics, and environmental management.
ELECTRICITY ACT, 2003
The Electricity Act, 2003 (“Electricity Act”) was enacted to regulate the generation, transmission, distribution, trading and use of
electricity by authorising a person to carry on the above acts either by availing a license or by seeking an exemption unde r the
Electricity Act. Additionally, the Electricity Act states no person other than Central Transmission Utility or State Tra nsmission
Utility, or a licensee shall transmit or use electricity at a rate exceeding 250 watts and 100 volts in any street or place
which is a factory within the meaning of the Factories Act, 1948 or a mine within the meaning of the Mines Act, 1952 or any place
in which 100 or more persons are ordinarily likely to be assembled. An exception to the said rule is given by stating that the applicant
shall apply by giving not less than 7 days’ notice in writing of his intention to the Electrical Inspector and to the District Magistrate
or the Commissioner of Police, as the case may be, containing the particulars of electrical installation and plant, if any, the nature
and purpose of supply of such electricity. The Electricity Act also lays down the requirement of mandatory use of meters to regulate
the use of electricity and authorises the Commission so formed under the Electricity Act, to determine the tariff for such usage.
The Electricity Act also authorises the State Government to grant subsidy to the consumers or class of consumers it deems fit from
paying the standard tariff required to be paid.

BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS ACT, 2016
Bureau, processes, systems and services, and formatters connected therewith and incidental thereto. Functions of the BIS incl ude,
inter alia, (a) recognizing as an Indian standard, with the prior approval of the Central Government, the mark of any interna tional
body or institution at par with the standard mark, for such goods, articles, process, system or service in India or elsewhere ; (b)
specifying a standard mark to be called the Bureau of Indian Standards Certification Mark which shall be of such design and contain
such particulars as maybe prescribed to represent a particular Indian standard; (c) providing training services in relation to inter alia,
quality management, standards, conformity of Indian Standards Act, 2016 provides for the establishment o f the Bureau of Indian
Standards (“BIS”) for the development of the activities, inter alia, standardization, conformity assessment and quality assur ance of
goods, articles assessment; (d) publishing Indian standards; promotion of safety in connection with any goods, article, process,
system or service; and (e) any such other functions as may be necessary for promotion, monitoring and management of the quali ty
of goods, articles, processes, systems and services and to protect the interests of consumers and o ther stakeholders.
BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS RULES, 2018 (THE “BUREAU OF INDIAN STANDARDS RULES”)
The Bureau of India Standards Rules, 2018, as amended, have been notified, in supersession of the Bureau of Indian Standards
Rules, 1987, in so far as they relate to Chapter IV A of the said rules relating to registration of the articles notified by the Central
Government, and in supersession of the Bureau of Indian Standards Rules, 2017 except in relation to things done or omitted to be
done before such supersession. Under the Bureau of Indian Standards Rules, the bureau is required to establish Indian sta ndards in
relation to any goods, article, process, system or service and shall reaffirm, amend, revise or withdraw Indian standards so
established as may be necessary.
THE LEGAL METROLOGY ACT, 2009 (“LEGAL METROLOGY ACT”) AND LEGAL METROLOGY (PACKAGED
COMMODITIES) RULES, 2011
The Legal Metrology Act was enacted to establish and enforce standards of weights and measures and to regulate trade and
commerce in weights, measures and other goods which are sold or distributed by weight, measure or number. It repealed and
replaced the Standard of Weights and Measures Act, 1976 and the Standards of Weights and Measures (Enforcement) Act, 1985.
Making use of any numeration not in accordance with the standards of weights and measures prescribed under the Legal Metrology
Act may be punished by a fine which may extend to ₹25,000 and for the second or subsequent offense, with imprisonment for a
term not exceeding six months and also with fine. Any transaction, deal or contract in contravention of the standards of weights and
measures prescribed by the government may be punished with fine which may extend to ₹ 10,000 and for the second or subsequent
offence, with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or both. The Legal Metrology Act permits th e
central government to make rules thereunder to carry out provisions of the Act. Further, states may, after consultation with the
central government, frame state specific rules under this Act to provide for the time limits for verification of weights and measures,
maintenance of registers and records, manner of notifying government authorities, fees for compounding of offences etc.
The Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) Rules, 2011 framed under the Legal Metrology Act lay down specific provisions
applicable to packages intended for retail sale, wholesale packages and for export of packaged commodities and also provide f or
registration of manufacturers, packers and importers. Also, the Legal Metrology (Government Approved Test Centre) Rules, 2013
have laid down specifications about verification of weights and measures specified therein by government approved test centre .
THE FACTORIES ACT, 1948
The Factories Act, 1948 (“Factories Act”) seeks to regulate labour employed in factories and makes provisions for the safety, health
and welfare of the workers. An occupier of a factory under the Factories Act, means the person who has ultimate control ove r the
affairs of the factory. The occupier or manager of the factory is required to obtain a registration for the factory. The Fact ories Act
also requires inter alia the maintenance of various registers dealing with safety, labour standards, holidays and extent of child labour
including their conditions. Further, notice of accident or dangerous occurrence in the factory is to be provided to the insp ector by
the manager of the factory. The Factories Act requires that the occupier of a factory, i.e., the person who has ultimate control
over the affairs of the factory and inthe case of a company, any one of the directors, must ensure the health, safety and welfare
of all workers especially in respect of safety and proper maintenance of the fa ctory, such that it does not pose health risks, the safe
use, handling, storage and transport of factory articles and substances, provision of adequate instruction, traini ng and
supervision to ensure workers’ health and safety, cleanliness and safe working conditions. The Factories Act also provides for fines
to be paid and imprisonment of the manager of the factory in case of any contravention of the provisions of the Factories Act .
